request_intro: Create the input image again in the art style that this specification defines. {rule:build_on_image} When the input shows a real place in focus (a room, a street, a building, a landscape), keep that place. A wall, curtain, or backdrop in focus behind the subjects is their place: keep it. When its background is even, featureless, or blurred, or shows only a floor under the subject, build the setting of the card around the subject, so that it carries the subject's emotion. Design the light and the composition to a professional standard. {rule:true_reflections}
precedence_note: The style specification has priority over the scene concept. Every rule of the specification stays in force, also for camera, format, framing, lighting key, empty space, and a place that the specification keeps; adapt or drop any part of the scene concept that conflicts with it.
open_slot_note: Some lines of the card are open slots: fill each open slot yourself with one concrete idea that grows from what the image already shows and fits the setting and the style. {rule:natural_surprise} {rule:in_place}

plots.text: a gift for the subject is left in a way that tells exactly who left it

plots.text: a household routine goes on, and the empty seat of one member still holds their things
an ordinary errand is half done, and its unfinished part waits beside the subject

the place puts itself back in order, and one object has returned to a slightly different spot

lines.label: Concept
lines.template: the picture shows what the input image shows. {rule:emotion_first} {rule:composition_first} Let the place, the light, and the colors carry that emotion. {rule:one_figure} {rule:uncanny_balance} Start the instruction with one plain sentence that tells what the picture shows

graphic.template: the picture shows the subject of the input image with its own emotion and pose, only with the shapes, marks, and colors that the specification allows; the symbol shows that emotion one step stronger, never another one. variants.template: each main character of the image (each person the picture is about, whom the viewer must recognize) gets a unique character design of the style, taken from that person: an own face shape, eye shape and eye size, brows, hairstyle silhouette, and body type, so that no two main characters share one face; every main character gets the large eyes of the style, larger than the eyes of the photo (each eye about as tall as the nose is long, the iris filling most of the eye); a main creature (a monster, an alien, a puppet) keeps the build of its own head from the input, one step stronger like a caricature: the outline of the head and where it is widest, the size and the place of the eyes, the size and the shape of the nose, the thickness of the lips, the chin and the jaw, and the outline of the hair; it takes only the line, the colors, and the eye construction of the style, never the face of the people; a person of a crowd or far in the background is a background extra of the style: simpler means fewer details and flatter color, never a broken drawing; each extra has a correct, complete body with natural proportions, a clear face of a few clean lines with both eyes and a mouth in place, whole hands, and whole, recognizable objects, drawn with the same clean line as the main characters; each extra sits fully in its own seat or place, and no extra is cut by a main character's head in a confusing way

slots.label: Backstory
slots.text: invent in one clause what happened just before this moment, and show one visible trace of it

slots.label: Outside the frame
slots.text: decide who or what is just outside the frame, and show one hint of it inside the frame, such as a shadow, a reflection, or an object that belongs to it

slots.label: Private detail
slots.text: add one small detail that only the subject would notice, close to the subject

slots.label: Tie object
slots.text: choose the object that ties the scene to a story, and make it the clearest prop near the subject

slots.label: Next second

slots.label: Owner
slots.text: decide who lives or works in this place, and show two objects that tell it

slots.label: House rule

slots.label: Season

slots.label: Sound

slots.label: Reward

slots.label: Memory

slots.label: Sign
slots.text: choose one signature detail of the subject that carries the concept, in the form that the specification allows

slots.label: Motif choice

slots.label: Context mark

slots.label: Scent
slots.text: decide the strongest smell of this place, and show its source near the subject

slots.label: Touch
slots.text: decide how one surface near the subject feels to the touch, and make that texture clear

slots.label: Weight
slots.text: decide which thing near the subject is the heaviest or the lightest, and show that weight in how it rests on its support

slots.label: Wish
slots.text: decide what this subject would want most in this moment, and show the wanted thing in view but out of reach

slots.label: Favorite thing
slots.text: decide which thing in this place belongs most to the subject, and give it the best spot near the subject

slots.label: Last visitor
slots.text: decide who came to this place last, and show the one thing that they left behind

slots.label: Oldest thing
slots.text: add one thing that is much older than everything else in this place, and show one sign of how it survived

slots.label: Unfinished thing
slots.text: leave one thing in this place unfinished, and let its missing part show what it will become

slots.label: Motion
slots.text: choose one small thing that moves near the still subject, and show the direction of its movement

slots.label: Scale clue
slots.text: add one familiar thing whose size shows how big or how small the subject is

slots.label: Counterpart
slots.text: add one small element that is the opposite of the subject in shape or color, never a second figure, and place it so that the two complete each other, in a form that the specification allows

slots.label: Hidden answer
slots.text: decide what question this picture asks, and hide its answer in one small detail far from the subject, in a form that the specification allows

lines.label: Homage

variants.template: blend partial motifs from one to three well-known films, series, books, games, or paintings that you choose, which match these traits of the specification: {style:influences*2-3}, its aesthetic and mood, and this setting. Put the borrowed motifs at these places: {lib:landings*1-3}. Take a different kind of element from each work and transform it, so that the image stays original and only feels familiar. Leave out characters, names, logos, and text of these works, and {rule:no_titles}; {rule:ordinary_motifs}

let one well-known film, series, book, game, or painting that you choose give most motifs of this picture. Choose a work that matches these traits of the specification: {style:influences*2-3}, its aesthetic and mood, and this setting. Put its motifs at these places: {lib:landings*1-2}. Transform each motif under the rules of the specification, so that the image stays original and only feels familiar. Leave out characters, names, logos, and text of the work, and {rule:no_titles}; {rule:ordinary_motifs}

Put the borrowed motifs at these places: {lib:landings*1-3}. Take a different kind of element from each work and transform it, so that the image stays original and only feels familiar. Leave out characters, names, logos, and text of these works, and {rule:no_titles}; {rule:ordinary_motifs}

lines.label: Story homage
lines.template: take one story situation, relationship, or twist from a well-known film, series, book, game, or painting that you choose, which matches these traits of the specification: {style:influences*1-2}. Stage it around the subject in its own pose as an enrichment of this card, transformed so that the image stays original. Leave out characters, names, logos, and text of the work, and {rule:no_titles}; {rule:ordinary_motifs}
lines.fallback_template: take one story situation, relationship, or twist from a well-known film, series, book, game, or painting that you choose, which matches the influences, the aesthetic, and the mood of the specification. Stage it around the subject in its own pose as an enrichment of this card, transformed so that the image stays original. Leave out characters, names, logos, and text of the work, and {rule:no_titles}; {rule:ordinary_motifs}

one_figure.text: The subject is the only figure in the picture, unless the specification or the input image shows other people or creatures: tell of anyone else only by traces, such as an object, an open door, a lit window, or a shadow at the edge, never by a visible person, figure, or silhouette.

true_reflections.text: Every reflection in a mirror, glass, metal, or water obeys the geometry of the place: the surface shows what stands in front of it, from its own position and angle (a floor puddle shows the subject upside down from below, a side mirror the side that faces it, a mirror or a window behind the subject its back), mirrored, in the perspective of the scene, and changed by its material, never a flat copy of the subject; a wrong reflection changes the place, the light, or one object, and the subject in it keeps the same pose.

no_titles.text: never write the title of a work or the name of its author in the instruction: describe only the borrowed motifs

ordinary_motifs.text: each borrowed motif becomes an ordinary thing that belongs to this place and this moment, so that the work is felt in the mood, the light, and the colors, never seen as a famous prop quoted as it is

surprise_logic.text: in the logic of the style (quietly strange in an uncanny style, enigmatic in a mysterious one, magical in a fantasy one, playful in a comic one, warm in a cozy one)

second_look.text: everything else stays true to the world of the style, so that the surprise shows on a second look

natural_surprise.text: An unexpected element follows the logic of the style and is treated as natural in its world, never a random sight gag.

uncanny_balance.text: Keep the balance of the style: at most one quiet strangeness, and everything else believable, so that the picture reads as real at first glance.

build_on_image.text: The input image is already the story: keep its subjects, their poses and expressions, the people it shows, its place, and its composition. The composition is the subjects, the place, and the shot, never the faults of the photo: an out-of-focus object at an edge, a dark or cut corner, a vignette, a lens flare, or a finger over the lens; the picture shows its scene to every edge and corner. Build the picture over it: redraw everything in the style, simplify the over-detailed areas, and add details of the style only where the image is plain, blurred, or empty, in the tone of the subject's emotion and of its place. Never add a new plot, event, character, or object that the image does not suggest.

in_place.text: Every added thing belongs to the place, at the position where such a thing usually is (on furniture, a wall, a sill, the ground farther away); never a group of things set down around the subject.

in_place_short.text: only at the place where such a thing usually is, never as a group of things around the subject

emotion_first.text: Read the emotion of each person or animal in the image and keep it: show it one step stronger with the means of acting that the style has (eyes, mouth, brows, hands, the line of the body), never as another emotion.

composition_first.text: Keep the composition of the image (the same subjects, their places in the frame, their size in the frame, and the shot), and make it read as a strong shot of the style: the main subjects clear and readable, the secondary ones simpler, and the background in clear planes. Keep the color key of the image (a cool place stays cool, a warm one stays warm, each main color keeps its hue) and make it clean, clear, and bright in the means of the style; drop only the blur and the color cast of the photo (a tint of the camera or of a colored lamp over the whole frame); the own color of a surface (a blue door, a gray pavement, a green field) is never a cast and keeps its hue and temperature, and lift a dull, underexposed photo; a scene that is dark by its nature (a cinema, a candle-lit room, a night street) keeps its low key, with the light on the faces and the light sources.

recipes.name: quiet moment
recipes.note: keep this picture calm and simple: few elements and much breathing space; the light, the place, and one or two details tell the story

recipes.name: story-led
recipes.note: let the story read at a glance: the subject and the main story element form one clear moment that a viewer can retell in one sentence

recipes.name: homage-led
recipes.note: let the borrowed motifs carry the atmosphere: mood, light, and color first, objects last

recipes.name: surprise-led
recipes.note: build the picture around its one surprise; every other part stays plain, so that the surprise reads

recipes.name: plot-led
recipes.note: let the plot carry the picture: a viewer sees the setup and the turn at one glance and can retell the plot in one sentence

recipes.name: before and after
recipes.note: show the plot as a before and an after in one picture: the trace of what came before is far from the subject, and the result is next to it

recipes.name: small drama
recipes.note: stage the plot as a small drama with a clear cause and effect: the subject stays the calm center while the place reacts

recipes.name: quiet chapter
recipes.note: tell the plot quietly, as one page of a longer story: few elements, calm space, and one clear trace of what came before

recipes.name: two scales
recipes.note: tell the concept twice, at two scales: the big place around the subject and a small copy of the same story inside it, close to the subject. The small world has no figures, and the viewer finds it on a second look.

recipes.name: ritual
recipes.note: tell the concept as a small ritual of this place: the objects of the ritual stand around the subject in a careful order. The order alone shows that the ritual happens again and again.

recipes.name: aftermath
recipes.note: tell the concept through the moment just after something big happened, and keep the event itself out of view. Its traces lie around the calm subject, and the viewer guesses the event from them.

recipes.name: discovery
recipes.note: tell the concept as a discovery: something that this place hid comes to light right next to the subject. The found thing is the clearest point of the picture, and the light and the lines of the place lead the eye to it.

recipes.name: the place as a character
recipes.note: let the place answer the presence of the subject with one small sign of its own parts, as if the place were a second character, {rule:surprise_logic}. The sign is a shape or a small object, never a new light or a new color: the place keeps the light and the color temperature of the input. The place never gets a face or a body, and everything else in it stays believable.

recipes.name: within reach
recipes.note: tell the whole story with the things within reach of the subject, in the closest frame that the specification allows. The far setting stays soft and simple, and every detail near the subject counts.

recipes.name: quiet triumph
recipes.note: tell the concept as the moment just after a small success of the subject. The proof of the success sits near the subject, and the calm scene honors it without a celebration.

recipes.name: interrupted moment
recipes.note: tell the concept as an interrupted moment: an activity around the subject stops halfway and leaves its objects in the foreground. The cause of the interruption shows only as a hint at the edge of the frame.

recipes.name: collection
recipes.note: tell the concept through a collection or a series: one form repeats many times in a clear order around the subject. The order breaks once, near the subject, and that break carries the story.

recipes.name: threshold
recipes.note: tell the concept as the start of a journey: the subject keeps its place on the near side of a threshold, and the far side opens deep into the picture. The near side shows where the subject comes from, and the far side promises where it goes.

recipes.name: warm and cold
recipes.note: tell the concept as a meeting of warm and cold: the subject belongs to one color temperature and the place around it to the other, by light where the specification has light and by color in every case. One element carries a little of the other temperature across, toward the subject.
